text: For a group \(G\) let \(D_n(G)=G\cap(1+\Delta(G)^n)\) be its integral dimension subgroups and \(\gamma_n(G)\) its lower central series. Whether \(D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)\) for every group is open (Kourovka Notebook, Problem 20.84). For Lie rings the analogous inclusion was recently proved by Ionin, Mikhailov and Petrov, and formally verified in Lean. This note collects what is known, records an elementary reduction of the group question to finite metabelian \(2\)-groups of class three, analyses which steps of the Lie-ring proof have no group-theoretic counterpart, and reports computational evidence: a computer search shows that a counterexample among finite \(2\)-groups of class three has order at least \(2^{12}\). For \(3\)-torsion in \(D_5/\gamma_5\) we prove \(D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)\) whenever \(G/\gamma_2(G)\) is finite and has at most one invariant larger than \(3\), and, with a computer search, for all \(3\)-groups of order at most \(3^9\). We do not solve the problem.

Status markers. [Lean] formally verified; [paper] proved on paper (here or in the cited source); [computer] checked by computation; [open] open. Combined markers such as [computer + paper] mean that the argument uses both; further text inside a marker qualifies it.

Let \(\Delta=\Delta(G)\) be the augmentation ideal of \(\mathbb{Z}[G]\) and \(D_n(G)=\{g\in G: g-1\in\Delta^n\}\). Always \(\gamma_n(G)\subseteq D_n(G)\) [paper; Lean: §4], with equality for \(n\le 3\) and failure for \(n=4\) in general (Rips [Rip72]).
Question ( [KM26, Problem 20.84], [IMP26, §1.3]). Is \(D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)\) for every group \(G\)? [open]

Known facts used below (all [paper], from the cited sources): \(D_4(G)^2\subseteq\gamma_4(G)\) (Passi [Pas68], see also [MP09]); \(D_n(G)/\gamma_n(G)\) is abelian [GK92]; the exponent of \(D_5(G)/\gamma_5(G)\) divides \(3!=6\) (Tahara [Tah81, Cor. 6.11], proved there for finite groups, to which the general case reduces by the standard argument; Tahara also gives an explicit description of \(D_5\) for finite groups of class \(4\) [Tah81, Thm. 6.1] and shows \(D_k=\gamma_k\) for \(k\le5\) when \(G\) has no elements of order \(2\) or \(3\) [Tah81, Cor. 6.12]); Gupta's claim that all \(D_n/\gamma_n\) are \(2\)-groups [Gup02] is false: Bartholdi and Mikhailov constructed a \(3\)-group with \(D_7\neq\gamma_7\) [BM23]. See also our analysis of Gupta's argument in the project tracker, D5-22.

Proposition. The following are equivalent. • \(D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)\) for every group \(G\). • \(D_5(M)=1\) for every metabelian group \(M\) of nilpotency class at most \(3\). • \(D_5(Q)=1\) for every finite metabelian \(2\)-group \(Q\) of nilpotency class exactly \(3\).
Proof. (In Lean with the theorems of Passi and Gruenberg and \(D_3=\gamma_3\) as explicit hypotheses, and with “metabelian” dropped by Remark 2.2, see §4.)
\((1)\Rightarrow(3)\) is clear since \(\gamma_4(Q)=1\).

\((2)\Rightarrow(1)\). Put \(N=\gamma_4(G)G''\). Since \(G''=[\gamma_2(G),\gamma_2(G)]\subseteq\gamma_4(G)\), \(N=\gamma_4(G)\), and \(M=G/N\) is metabelian of class \(\le 3\). The projection \(\pi\colon G\to M\) induces a ring map \(\mathbb{Z}[G]\to\mathbb{Z}[M]\) sending \(\Delta(G)^n\) into \(\Delta(M)^n\), so \(\pi(D_5(G))\subseteq D_5(M)=1\), i.e. \(D_5(G)\subseteq N=\gamma_4(G)\). (This is the group version of the step from Theorem C to Corollary D in [IMP26].)

\((3)\Rightarrow(2)\). Let \(M\) be metabelian of class \(\le3\) and \(1\ne x\in D_5(M)\). Finite generation. \(x-1\) is a finite \(\mathbb{Z}\)-linear combination of products \((g_1-1)\cdots(g_5-1)\); all \(g_i\) and \(x\) lie in a finitely generated subgroup \(H\), and then \(x\in D_5(H)\). \(H\) is metabelian of class \(\le 3\), hence finitely generated nilpotent. Exponent two. By Passi, \(D_4(H)^2\subseteq\gamma_4(H)=1\); as \(D_5\subseteq D_4\), \(x^2=1\). Finite \(2\)-quotients. Let \(T\) be the (finite, normal) subgroup of elements of odd order of \(H\); \(x\notin T\). The group \(H/T\) is finitely generated nilpotent with \(2\)-group torsion, hence residually a finite \(2\)-group (Gruenberg [Gru57]). Choose a finite \(2\)-group quotient \(Q\) of \(H\) in which the image of \(x\) is nontrivial; by functoriality it lies in \(D_5(Q)\). \(Q\) is metabelian of class \(\le 3\), and class \(\le 2\) is impossible because then \(D_5(Q)\subseteq D_3(Q)=\gamma_3(Q)=1\).

Remark (“metabelian” is automatic). Every group of nilpotency class \(\le 3\) is metabelian: \(G''=[\gamma_2(G),\gamma_2(G)]\subseteq\gamma_4(G)\) by P. Hall's inclusion \([\gamma_i,\gamma_j]\subseteq\gamma_{i+j}\) (see e.g. [MP09]); this is the same fact used in \((2)\Rightarrow(1)\). So in (2) and (3) the word “metabelian” may be dropped: (3) is the statement that \(D_5(Q)=1\) for every finite \(2\)-group of class \(3\), and the search space of §5 is simply the \(2\)-groups of class \(3\). The same holds for Lie rings (\([\gamma_2,\gamma_2]\subseteq\gamma_4\)), so Theorem C of [IMP26] for \(c=3\) needs no metabelian hypothesis either; the hypothesis matters only for \(c\ge4\), where \(D_{2c-1}=1\) for all groups of class \(\le c\) is a different, stronger question. This standard fact was noticed again only while setting up the ANUPQ search (D5-24), where the option Metabelian cut nothing. [paper]

Remark (a bounded form). For finite groups the proof gives more. If \(G\) is finite then so are \(M=G/\gamma_4(G)\) and \(H\le M\), and one may take \(Q=H/T\), a finite \(2\)-group whose order is the \(2\)-part of \(|H|\), hence divides the \(2\)-part of \(|G|\). Therefore: if \(D_5(Q)=1\) for all metabelian \(2\)-groups \(Q\) of class \(3\) and order \(\le 2^k\), then \(D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)\) for every finite group \(G\) whose Sylow \(2\)-subgroup has order \(\le 2^k\) [paper; Lean] (in Lean Gruenberg's theorem is not needed: there \(H=M\), and \(Q\) is the Sylow \(2\)-subgroup of \(M\), a direct factor since \(M\) is nilpotent; for \(Q\) of class \(\le3\) Passi's theorem is the only hypothesis, for class exactly \(3\) also \(D_3=\gamma_3\)). Note that the exponent step uses Passi's theorem for \(H\) (where \(\gamma_4(H)=1\)), not for an arbitrary group.

Remark. Proposition 2.1(2) is precisely the group analogue of Theorem C of [IMP26] for \(c=3\) (“a metabelian Lie ring of class \(\le c\) has \(D_{2c-1}=0\)”). The reduction is elementary and almost certainly known to experts; we record it because it fixes the search space for computations (§5).

We summarise the proof of [IMP26, Theorem C, Corollary D], checked against the text ([paper]; the final statements are [Lean], audited in the project tracker, D5-23). • Reduction to \(L\) metabelian of class \(\le c\) (Corollary 6.14) and to finitely generated \(L\) (Lemma 6.13). Transfers: this is Proposition 2.1. • A central extension \(0\to K\to T\to L\to0\), \(T=L\times_{L_{ab}}P\) with \(P\) free abelian, such that \(\gamma_i(T)\cong\gamma_i(L)\) for \(i\ge2\) and \(T\cong T'\oplus P\) additively (Lemma 6.4, Corollary 6.7). • The integral PBW theorem: \(\mathrm{gr}\,U(T)\cong\mathrm{Sym}_\mathbb{Z}(T)\) and, for \(T\) a direct sum of cyclic groups, an explicit \(\mathbb{Z}\)-basis of ordered monomials with known additive orders (Theorem 2.3, Corollary 2.4). • The additive projection \(p\colon U(T)\to P_{\le2}U(T)\) onto monomials of length \(\le 2\) (§6.2), and a retraction \(r\colon P_{\le2}U(T)\to T\) killing \(Z(T)\cdot T\) (Lemma 5.3). • The quadratic part of \(p(\varpi(T)^n)\) lies in \(\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(T)\gamma_j(T)\) (Proposition 6.12); for \(n=2c-1\) every such term has a central factor, and Theorem 5.1 gives \(D_{2c-1}(L)=0\).
section: 3. The Lie-ring proof and where it does not transfer

text: Obstacles for groups (our analysis; [paper] where a source is cited, otherwise an explanation, not a theorem): • No PBW basis of the required kind. Step 3 is the heart of the argument: it gives an additive splitting of \(U(T)\) by monomial length, compatible with additive orders, so that “the quadratic part” of an element is well defined and computable. For \(\mathbb{Z}[G]\) the filtration by powers of \(\Delta\) has associated graded ring \(\bigoplus\Delta^n/\Delta^{n+1}\), which in general is not the integral enveloping algebra of \(\mathrm{gr}\,\gamma_\bullet(G)\); over \(\mathbb Q\) the analogous comparison is Quillen's theorem [Qui68], and over \(\mathbb{Z}\) its failure is essentially the dimension subgroup problem itself (cf. [HMP07,MP09]). There is no canonical additive projection of \(\mathbb{Z}[G]\) onto “length \(\le 2\)”. • The extension \(T\). Step 2 has a formal group analogue (pull back a free abelian cover of \(G_{ab}\) along \(G\to G_{ab}\), giving a central extension with the same higher lower central terms). What is missing is how to use it: in the Lie case \(T'\) is an additive direct summand and its elements commute in \(U(T)\), which drives the rewriting Lemmas 6.9–6.10. In \(\mathbb{Z}[G]\) products of commutators do not commute and the corresponding rewriting produces higher-order terms (“collection”). • Torsion is already there in degree four. For Lie rings \(D_n=\gamma_n\) for \(n\le3\) and \(2D_4\subseteq\gamma_4\) [BP15], the same pattern as for groups; but for groups even the description of \(D_4/\gamma_4\) requires the full Rips–Passi machinery, and the known group computations of \(D_5\) (e.g. the group of [IMP26, §3.3], where \(D_5(G)=\langle w\rangle\subseteq\gamma_4(G)\)) are case-by-case.
section: 3. The Lie-ring proof and where it does not transfer

text: The Lean 4 project group-dimension (Mathlib v4.29.0, the version used by [IMP26]) defines \(\Delta(G)\) as the kernel of the augmentation of MonoidAlgebra \(\mathbb{Z}\) \(G\) and \(D_n(G)=\{g: g-1\in\Delta^n\}\), with literature indexing; Mathlib's lowerCentralSeries G k is \(\gamma_{k+1}\). The following are proved, with no sorry and only the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound [Lean]: • \(D_n(G)\) is a normal subgroup, \(D_0=D_1=G\), the series is decreasing, and \(\Delta^i\Delta^j\subseteq\Delta^{i+j}\); • the commutator identities \([a,b]-1=a^{-1}b^{-1}\big((a-1)(b-1)-(b-1)(a-1)\big)\) (for \([a,b]=a^{-1}b^{-1}ab\)) and its analogue for Mathlib's convention; consequently \([D_i,D_j]\subseteq D_{i+j}\) and \(\gamma_n(G)\subseteq D_n(G)\); • functoriality of \(D_n\) under group homomorphisms; • \(D_2(G)=\gamma_2(G)\), via a ring map \(\mathbb{Z}[G]\to\mathbb{Z}\oplus G_{ab}\) (square-zero extension) killing \(\Delta^2\); • Proposition 2.1 and Remark 2.3: first, \(D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)\) for all \(G\) iff \(D_5(Q)=1\) for all \(Q\) of class \(\le 3\); then, with Passi's \(D_4^2\subseteq\gamma_4\) and Gruenberg's theorem as explicit hypotheses, iff \(D_5(Q)=1\) for all finite \(2\)-groups of class \(\le3\), and with \(D_3=\gamma_3\) also of class exactly \(3\); the bounded form for finite \(G\) does not need Gruenberg's theorem; “metabelian” is dropped by Remark 2.2, which is not formalized (dimensionQuestion5_iff_finite_two_groups, dimensionQuestion5_iff_class_three, D_five_le_of_bounded, D_five_le_of_bounded_class_three; file FiniteReduction.lean). Finite generation is proved: every element of \(\Delta(G)^n\) comes from \(\Delta(H)^n\) for a finitely generated \(H\le G\); • Lemma 5.9 (adjoining a central root): \(\mathbb{Z}[H]\cap\Delta(K)^n=\Delta(H)^n\) and \(D_n(K)=D_n(H)\) for \(n\ge2\) (D_n_eq_of_index, file CentralRoot.lean); • Proposition 5.8, all cases, with the ring statement \(\mathbb{Z}[H]\cap\Delta(Q)^n=\Delta(H)^n\), for \(Q=H\langle a,b\rangle\) with \(a,b\) centralising \(H\) and \(a,b,ab\notin H\); also the step of adjoining a central square root in (2) and the variant \(c^{2^j}\in\gamma_{j+2}(H)\) (D_n_eq_of_dihedral, D_n_eq_of_sqrt, D_n_eq_of_central_product and its corollaries; files CentralD8.lean, CentralSqrt.lean, CentralProduct.lean). The passage from \((H\times E)/\{(\varphi(z),z^{-1})\}\) to this form and the classification of \(E\) are not formalized. The formal proof uses the same overgroup \((Q\times\mathbb{Z})/\langle(s,-2)\rangle\) for \(Q_8\) and \(M_{2^{k+2}}\), with \(s=a^2\) (\(s=t\) for \(Q_8\)) and \(b^2=s^e\) (\(e=1\) for \(Q_8\), \(e=0\) for \(M_{2^{k+2}}\)): the image \(\zeta\) of the generator of \(\mathbb{Z}\) has \(\zeta^2=s\), and \(a\zeta^{-1}\), \(b\zeta^{-e}\) generate a subgroup \(D_8\) centralising \(H\langle\zeta\rangle\); • Lemma 6.3 and Proposition 6.5, with \(d(Q)\) the least number of generators (commutator_gamma_two_le_gamma_five, metabelian_of_class_four, card_ge_of_not_metabelian, metabelian_of_card_le, rank_of_card_nine, type_of_card_nine; files ClassFour.lean, ClassFourOrder.lean); in the proposition the class is assumed \(\le4\) instead of \(=4\). Instead of the Lie ring \(L(G)\) the proof works in \(G/\gamma_5(G)\), where \(\gamma_4\) is central: the brackets become \(F([a,b])\) for an additive \(F\colon\gamma_4\to\mathbb F_p\), nonzero at a given commutator (it exists since \(\gamma_4(G/\gamma_5)\) has exponent \(p\)), and both Jacobi identities come from the Hall–Witt identity. Also proved on the way: \([\gamma_i,\gamma_j]\subseteq\gamma_{i+j}\), a group of order \(p^n\) is generated by \(n\) elements, and in a finite \(p\)-group \(H\gamma_2=G\) implies \(H=G\). That both types occur for \(p=3\) is a computation and is not formalized; • Tahara's Theorem 6.1 [Tah81], the inclusion: for a finite group of class \(\le4\) and any uniqueness bases (with no basis element in the next term of the series) with their structure constants, \(D_5\) lies in the subgroup generated by the elements \(g\) over the integer families satisfying (A)–(F); the bases, structure constants, conditions and generators are written out as in [Tah81, pp. 143, 150, 159–161] (taharaFiveOne proves TaharaFiveOne; file TaharaTheorem.lean, proof in TaharaProof/). The proof follows §§2–6 of [Tah81]: the uniqueness bases of the layers are glued into one ordered family with normal forms, the basic products form a \(\mathbb{Z}\)-basis of \(\mathbb{Z}[G]\), and \(\Delta^n\) is spanned by the products of weight \(\ge n\) modulo lower ones; hence \(D_3=\gamma_3\) for these groups (Tahara's Theorem 4.1), and the map \(\psi_3\) of Tahara's Theorem 5.1 into \(W_3^*\oplus W_4\), with Losey's basis, sends \(\Delta^5\) into the span \(R_5^*\) of the relations (I)–(VII). For \(g\in D_5\) the coordinates of \(\psi_3(g-1)\) give (A)–(F), and its \(A_3\oplus A_4\) part identifies \(g\) with a generator. The Lean statement of condition (C\(_2\)) was checked against [Tah81, p. 160]; • Theorems 6.6 and 6.8, with no hypotheses (D_five_eq_gamma_five_of_exp_three, D_five_eq_gamma_five_of_cubes_cyclic; file TaharaTheorem.lean). They are proved with Tahara's Theorem 6.1 as an explicit hypothesis (D_five_eq_gamma_five, D_five_eq_gamma_five_cyclic; files ExpThree.lean, ExpThreePlus.lean), and the hypothesis is discharged by the previous item. In Theorem 6.8 the hypothesis reads “\(G/\gamma_2\) is a finite \(3\)-group whose cubes form a cyclic group”, which for a finite abelian \(3\)-group means at most one invariant \(>3\). The reduction to the finite group \(G/\gamma_5\) is proved too. Elements of \(\gamma_3\) and \(\gamma_4\) are compared through additive maps to \(\mathbb F_3\), and the uniqueness bases adapted to the cube map come from bases of \(\mathbb F_3\)-spaces; • the Lie-ring inclusion \(D_5(L)\subseteq\gamma_4(L)\), derived from the authors' LieRings.Publication.corollaryD [IMP26]. Stated as named propositions with references, not proved: Question 1.1; \(D_3=\gamma_3\); \(D_4^2\subseteq\gamma_4\); Rips's example; Gruenberg's theorem [Gru57] in the form used in Proposition 2.1; Tahara's bound; the two Gupta–Kuz'min statements of [GK92]; \(D_5^2\subseteq G''\gamma_5\) [MP09, Thm. 2.28]; and the group analogues of Theorem C and Corollary D of [IMP26] (without any claim about their truth). Some of them are explicit hypotheses of theorems (as in Proposition 2.1); none is assumed globally.
All code, raw tables and the checks are in compute/ of the repository https://github.com/ispacex/dimension-subrings (README.md, results/SUMMARY.md).

Method. For finite \(G\), \(\Delta\) is free abelian with basis \(\{g-1\}_{g
e1}\), and \(\Delta^n=\mathrm{span}_\mathbb{Z}\{b(x_i-1): b 	ext{ in a basis of } \Delta^{n-1},\ x_i 	ext{ generators}\}\): no closure under further multiplication is needed, since \(\Delta\) is the left ideal generated by the \(x_i-1\) and \(\Delta^{n-1}\mathbb{Z}[G]=\Delta^{n-1}\). The lattices are computed in Howell form over \(\mathbb{Z}/p^E\) (\(E=30,19,13\) for \(p=2,3,5\)), which is exact for our purpose: \(g-1
otin\Delta^n+p^E\Delta\) implies \(g-1
otin\Delta^n\), and the equalities \(D_n=\gamma_n\) below are proved by such non-memberships (memberships are certified separately by \(p^{E-1}\Delta\subseteq\Delta^n+p^E\Delta\)). Groups are taken from the SmallGroups library [BEO02] of GAP [GAP]; each group is computed until \(D_n=1\).

Checks. \(\gamma_n\subseteq D_n\) at every level of every group; a second method (left multiplication on conjugacy-class representatives of a pc-generating set) on all groups of orders \(8\)–\(64\), \(81\), \(243\), \(625\); an independent exact Hermite normal form over \(\mathbb{Z}\) in PARI/GP [PARI] on all groups of orders \(8\)–\(64\), \(81\) and \(12\) groups of order \(128\); known values (\(\Delta^n/\Delta^{n+1}\cong G\) for cyclic \(G\), \(\Delta/\Delta^2\cong G_{ab}\)). No discrepancies.

Sieves (theorems, used to skip groups): \(p\)-class \(\ge\) class, so groups of \(p\)-class \(2\) have class \(\le2\); for \(2\)-groups of class \(3\), \(D_5\subseteq D_3=\gamma_3\), Jennings' theorem \(D_n\subseteq M_n\) (the mod-\(2\) dimension subgroups) and Passi's \(D_4^2\subseteq\gamma_4=1\) give \(D_5\subseteq\Omega_1(\gamma_3\cap M_5)\), so only groups with \(K=\Omega_1(\gamma_3\cap M_5)\ne1\) need the lattice; for \(3\)-groups of class \(4\) the analogous \(K=\Omega_1(\gamma_4\cap M_5)\), using \(D_4=\gamma_4\) for groups without \(2\)-torsion (from Passi's \(D_4^2\subseteq\gamma_4\) [Pas68]) and Tahara's bound \(D_5^6\subseteq\gamma_5\) [Tah81, Cor. 6.11] (both [paper]).

Proposition ([computer]). In each of the following groups \(D_n(G)=\gamma_n(G)\) for all \(n\): • all \(2\)-groups of order \(8,16,32,64,128\) (\(2665\) groups) and all groups of order \(256\) of class \(\ge3\) (\(24\,328\) groups); • all \(3\)-groups of order \(81\), \(243\), \(729\) (\(586\) groups); • all \(1202\) groups of order \(3^7\) of class \(4\) that pass the sieve (by two methods, the lattice of §5 and the truncated Magnus algebra of §7, item 1, with identical results); • all \(15\) groups of order \(625\) (a control). Every \(3\)-group of class \(4\) and order \(3^5\), \(3^6\), \(3^7\) (\(6\), \(71\), \(1309\) groups) is metabelian (this is proved in Proposition 6.5, also in Lean). Moreover, \(D_5(Q)=1\) for every metabelian group \(Q\) of order \(512\) and class \(3\): the sieve leaves \(2792\) of the \(1\,587\,389\) such groups (out of \(1\,708\,439\) groups of order \(512\) and \(p\)-class \(\ge 3\)), and for each of the \(2792\) the lattice computation gives \(D_4(Q)=D_5(Q)=1\).

Order \(2^{10}\). This order is not in SmallGroups, and generating all \(2\)-groups of class \(3\) of this order is out of reach: at rank \(\ge4\) the \(p\)-group generation tree has millions of nodes already at order \(2^9\). Instead, the complete result at order \(2^9\) cuts the search down to a few thousand candidates.

Notation. \(P_1(Q)=Q\), \(P_{i+1}(Q)=[P_i(Q),Q]\,P_i(Q)^2\) is the lower exponent-\(2\) central series, and the \(2\)-class of \(Q\) is the least \(c\) with \(P_{c+1}(Q)=1\); \(M_n(Q)=Q\cap(1+\Delta_{\mathbb F_2}(Q)^n)\) are the mod-\(2\) dimension subgroups, \(M_n=\prod_{i2^j\ge n}\gamma_i^{2^j}\) (Jennings [Jen41], Lazard [Laz54]). If \(Q\) has \(2\)-class \(c\ge2\), it is an immediate descendant of \(Q/P_c(Q)\) of step size \(\log_2|P_c(Q)|\); the \(p\)-group generation algorithm [OBr90], as implemented in ANUPQ [GNO], lists all immediate descendants of a given group of a given step size, up to isomorphism.

Lemma (minimal counterexample). Let \(Q\) be a finite \(2\)-group of class \(3\) such that \(D_5(Q/N)=1\) for every central subgroup \(N\) of order \(2\). If \(D_5(Q)\ne1\), then (a) \(Z(Q)\) is cyclic and \(D_5(Q)=\Omega_1(Z(Q))=\langle n\rangle\) has order \(2\); (b) \(n\in\gamma_3(Q)\cap M_5(Q)\); (c) the \(2\)-class \(c\) of \(Q\) is at least \(4\), and \(P_c(Q)=\langle n\rangle\); (d) \(Q\) is an immediate descendant of step size \(1\) of \(R=Q/\langle n\rangle\), a group of class \(2\) or \(3\) and \(2\)-class \(c-1\ge3\) with \(\gamma_3(R)\) cyclic.

Proof. (a) Let \(N\le Z(Q)\), \(|N|=2\). The projection \(Q\to Q/N\) maps \(D_5(Q)\) into \(D_5(Q/N)=1\), so \(D_5(Q)\subseteq N\). Hence a nontrivial \(D_5(Q)\) equals every central subgroup of order \(2\): there is only one, so \(\Omega_1(Z(Q))\) has order \(2\), the abelian \(2\)-group \(Z(Q)\) is cyclic, and \(D_5(Q)=\Omega_1(Z(Q))\). (b) \(D_5\subseteq D_3=\gamma_3\), and \(D_5(Q)\subseteq M_5(Q)\) because \(\mathbb{Z}[Q]\to\mathbb F_2[Q]\) maps \(\Delta^5\) into \(\Delta_{\mathbb F_2}^5\). (c) Since \(\gamma_i\subseteq P_i\) and \(P_i^2\subseteq P_{i+1}\), we have \(\gamma_i^{2^j}\subseteq P_{i+j}\), and \(i2^j\ge5\) implies \(i+j\ge4\). So \(M_5\subseteq P_4\), and \(1\ne n\in P_4(Q)\) gives \(c\ge4\). The subgroup \(P_c(Q)\) is nontrivial, central and elementary abelian, hence equal to \(\Omega_1(Z(Q))=\langle n\rangle\). (d) By (c), \(R=Q/P_c(Q)\), the step size is \(1\) and \(R\) has \(2\)-class \(c-1\ge3\). \(R\) has class \(\le3\); if \(R\) were abelian, then \(\gamma_2(Q)\subseteq\langle n\rangle\subseteq Z(Q)\) and \(Q\) would have class \(\le2\). Finally \(\gamma_3(R)\) is a quotient of \(\gamma_3(Q)\subseteq Z(Q)\), which is cyclic.
Proposition ([computer + paper]). \(D_5(Q)=1\) for every \(2\)-group \(Q\) of order \(2^{10}\) and class \(3\) (all of them are metabelian, Remark 2.2).

Proof. Let \(Q\) be such a group with \(D_5(Q)\ne1\). For every central \(N\) of order \(2\) the quotient \(Q/N\) has order \(2^9\) and class \(\le3\), so \(D_5(Q/N)=1\): by Proposition 5.1 for class \(3\), and since \(D_5\subseteq D_3=\gamma_3=1\) for class \(\le2\). By Lemma 5.2, \(Q\) is then isomorphic to an immediate descendant of step size \(1\) of a group \(R\) of order \(2^9\), of class \(2\) or \(3\) and \(2\)-class \(\ge3\), with \(\gamma_3(R)\) cyclic, and \(Q\) has class \(3\), cyclic centre, and its involution \(n\) of the centre lies in \(\gamma_3(Q)\cap M_5(Q)\). [computer] The SmallGroups library contains \(1\,422\,862\) such groups \(R\). For each, ANUPQ (GAP 4.15.1 [GAP], ANUPQ 3.3.2 [GNO]) lists the immediate descendants of step size \(1\) up to isomorphism, \(1\,819\,675\) groups in all; \(88\,809\) of them have class \(3\), and exactly \(3400\) of these have cyclic centre with involution in \(\gamma_3\cap M_5\) (by rank \(d(Q)=2,3,4,5,6\): \(15\), \(301\), \(2756\), \(319\), \(9\); none of rank \(7\)). For each of the \(3400\) the lattice computation of §5 gives \(D_4(Q)=D_5(Q)=1\), in fact \(D_n(Q)=\gamma_n(Q)\) for all \(n\). This contradicts \(D_5(Q)\ne1\).

Checks of the order-\(2^{10}\) search. The same pipeline at orders \(2^6,\dots,2^9\) (parents from SmallGroups of half the order) was compared with a direct pass over SmallGroups of that order: the numbers of class-\(3\) groups with \(|P_c|=2\) and \(2\)-class \(\ge4\) (\(3\), \(27\), \(320\), \(4185\)), of those with cyclic centre, and of the candidates (\(3\), \(11\), \(64\), \(308\)) agree, also rank by rank. A second lattice method (the truncated Magnus algebra of §7, item 1, run on a pc-presentation, so independent of the multiplication table) gives the same answer on \(3391\) of the \(3400\) candidates. The search took \(62.9\) CPU-hours in GAP and the lattices \(21.3\) CPU-hours. Code, the proof of the lemma, the per-chunk and per-candidate tables: compute/pq1024 (README.md, section “Result: order \(2^{10}\) is closed”, and results/).

Theorem ([computer + paper]). • \(D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)\) for every finite group \(G\) whose Sylow \(2\)-subgroup has order at most \(2^{10}\); in particular for every group of order less than \(2048\). • \(D_n(G)=\gamma_n(G)\) for all \(n\) and every finite group \(G\) of order less than \(512\). • \(D_5(G)/\gamma_5(G)\) has no \(3\)-torsion for every finite group \(G\) whose Sylow \(3\)-subgroup has order at most \(3^7\); in fact \(D_5(Q)=\gamma_5(Q)\) for every \(3\)-group \(Q\) of order at most \(3^7\). (Extended to \(3^9\) in Theorem 6.14.)

Proof. (1) is Remark 2.3 with Propositions 5.1 and 5.3: every metabelian \(2\)-group of class \(3\) and order \(\le 2^{10}\) is covered (orders \(\le2^8\) by the lattice for all groups, \(2^9\) by the sieve and the lattice, \(2^{10}\) by Lemma 5.2, ANUPQ and the lattice). For (2) and (3): a finite nilpotent group is the direct product of its Sylow subgroups and \(D_n\), \(\gamma_n\) respect direct products, and for non-nilpotent finite \(G\) one reduces to the nilpotent quotients \(G/\gamma_m(G)\) [paper; standard, see [MP09]]; groups of order \(<512\) have \(2\)-part \(\le2^8\), \(3\)-part \(\le3^5\) and \(p\)-part \(\le p^3\) for \(p\ge5\), where class \(\le2\) makes everything trivial. For the \(3\)-part in (3): if \(Q\) is a \(3\)-group of order \(\le3^7\), then \(Q/\gamma_5(Q)\) has class \(\le4\) and order \(\le3^7\), hence is metabelian (class \(\le3\) always is, Remark 2.2; class \(4\) by Proposition 5.1), and Gupta–Tahara [GT85, Thm. 3.2(c)] (\(D_{p+2}=\gamma_{p+2}\) for finitely generated metabelian \(p\)-groups, \(p\) odd) gives \(D_5(Q/\gamma_5)=1\), i.e. \(D_5(Q)\subseteq\gamma_5(Q)\). This replaces the lattice computation for the \(1202\) candidates of order \(3^7\) (of which item (3) of Proposition 5.1 had checked a sample). The reduction for non-nilpotent groups in (2)–(3) is the standard one and has not been written out here.

Observations. In every group of class \(c\) computed, \(D_{c+1}=1\) and \(D_k=\gamma_k\) at each step. For metabelian groups of class \(3\) the Jennings sieve removes almost everything (orders \(64\), \(128\), \(256\), \(512\): \(111/114\), \(1116/1137\), \(21\,105/21\,325\), \(1\,584\,597/1\,587\,389\)), and the survivors have \(D_4=1\) already. For \(3\)-groups of class \(4\) the sieve removes little (\(9/71\) at order \(729\), \(107/1309\) at order \(2187\)). Computing time: about \(3.6\) hours wall clock, about \(30\)–\(40\) CPU-hours.

Remark (pruning the generation tree; D5-25). Let \(Q\) be a finite \(2\)-group of class \(3\) with cyclic centre, \(d=d(Q)\), \(C=C_Q(\gamma_2(Q))\), \(X=\gamma_2(Q)/(\gamma_2(Q)\cap Z(Q))\). The commutator map \(X\times Q/C\to\gamma_3(Q)\) is a non-degenerate bilinear pairing into the cyclic group \(\gamma_3(Q)\le Z(Q)\); hence \(X\cong Q/C\), a quotient of \(Q_{ab}\), and \(X\) has rank \(\le\min(d,d(d-1)/2)\). If \(|\gamma_3(Q)|=2^e\), then \(Q_{ab}\) has two invariants \(\ge 2^e\) (the map \((u,v)\mapsto[u,v,z]\) factors through \(\Lambda^2Q_{ab}\)) and \(X\) has an element of order \(\ge 2^e\). For a minimal counterexample \(Q\) (Lemma 5.2) with central involution \(n\) this gives conditions on every quotient \(V=Q/N\) with \(N\le\Phi(Q)\) (with \(n\in N\le\Phi(Q)\) for the second), which pass to further quotients and so may be used to cut whole subtrees of the \(p\)-group generation tree: (i) there is a cyclic \(K\), \(\gamma_3(V)\le K\le\gamma_2(V)\cap Z(V)\), with \(\mathrm{rk}(\gamma_2(V)/K)\le\min(d,d(d-1)/2)\); (ii) for such a \(K\), \(|Q|\ge 2|K|\,|A\vee B\vee E_1|\,|A\vee V_{ab}\vee E_2|\), where \(A=\gamma_2(V)/K\), \(B=V/C_V(\gamma_2(V))\), \(E_1=\mathbb{Z}/2^{e_V+1}\), \(E_2=E_1^2\), \(2^{e_V}=|\gamma_3(V)|\), and \(\vee\) is the componentwise maximum of abelian invariants. In particular every such \(V\) of class \(3\) has \(d+4e_V+2\le\log_2|Q|\). [paper] (proofs in compute/pq2048/README.md). Condition (i) is vacuous for \(d\le3\) and below order \(2^{2d+1}\); condition (ii) is the one that cuts.
